title: fix(scripts): durability gate — batch 10: declare the seeder wrappers in DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES (#12981)
body:
Part of #12981 — batch 10, the programme's last step. One file:
`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs`.

## What landed

`DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES` now declares the two seeder wrappers the
`catch { return null; }` family is made of — `tryInsert` and `tryUpdate` — each
with the consequence text the violation message prints, plus a header section
recording why the raw ObjectQL verbs stay out and what the alternative costs.

This is the handover the instrument of record reserved for the end of the
programme, in its own words (`scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs`):

> The programme ends by adding the seeder-helper names (`tryInsert`/`tryUpdate`)
> to the gate's `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES` **with zero reds**, which is what
> keeps `scripts/durability-degradation.baseline.json` at its designed empty
> steady state.

Measured on this tree: zero reds, verdict line unchanged at
`29 durability-critical catch seam(s), all loud, rethrowing or propagating to
the caller (4 propagating, declared)`. The baseline stays empty and is not
touched. The census reading is byte-identical before and after (the census
copies the gate's vocabulary by value, on purpose).

**The entries are not unfireable.** A temporary fixture in which a caller
re-swallows the wrapper — `try { await tryInsert(...) } catch { }` — was written
to disk, measured, and deleted in the same command: the gate reports it, exit 1,
`guards : tryInsert() at line 4` with this entry's consequence text. Tree clean
afterwards (`git status --porcelain` empty). That is the ratchet this step buys:
the seeder family cannot regress into a caller-side silent swallow.

## The pre-answered branch: measured, and it resolves to "declaration only"

Triage's 14:30Z comment pre-answered one branch — whether the `catch` in
`packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts` hands the failure to the caller on every
path, because a `FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES` entry is legal only if it does.

**Measured: it does.** With a vocabulary name that matches the seam
(`insert`, as a probe) plus the entry
`packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts::handleKeysRequest` declaring
`[['deps.error', 'return']]`, the gate's `catchDeliversFailure()` proves every
path out of that catch delivers: the site drops out of the findings list
(36 -> 35) and the entry is **not** reported stale. So no repair is owed in
`packages/runtime` and this never became a two-lane card. That file is not
touched by this PR.

## Why the declaration is NOT in this PR — a third branch nobody pre-answered

The entry is legal only while some vocabulary name matches a seam inside that
function, and the two candidate widenings do not agree:

| widening | keys.ts entry | gate verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `tryInsert` + `tryUpdate` (this PR, the census's reserved handover) | **STALE** — `1 stale entr(ies) in FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES ... the declaration excuses nothing, so delete it` | exit 1 |
| bare `insert` (what the in-file annotation assumed) | legal, seam green | exit 1 — **36 quiet degradations in 30 files**, 35 in 29 with keys.ts declared |

The annotation in `keys.ts` says its entry belongs to "the LAST step ... the one
that widens `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`" *"because that vocabulary has no
`insert`"* — i.e. it assumed the widening would be `insert`. The census, written
under the ruling that set this programme up, says the opposite in as many words:
**do NOT add `insert`/`update` to the gate vocabulary (option C, refused by the
gate's own design)**. Both cannot be satisfied at once, and the measurement above
is why: `insert` is a 30-file repair programme, which is the very thing this card
exists to not do by accident.

So this PR lands the half that is ruled and measured green, and hands the other
half back as a decision rather than picking a design unasked. The three options,
their costs and a recommendation are in the report comment on #12981. The map's
new header records the measurement in the file, so the next author reads a number
instead of re-deriving one.

## Verification

output. Head `07dc31ca0`.

- `pnpm check:durability-log-level` — exit 0.
  `self-test (log-level rule): 63 case(s) passed`;
  `self-test (read-seam invention rule): 57 case(s) passed`; both partition
  floors unchanged (no self-test rows added, so no floor re-measure is owed).
- `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs --self-test` — exit 0 before and

  site(s) total`. Census reading byte-identical before/after (`diff` exit 0).
- Derived family, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo
  objectstack-ai/objectstack` re-derived after merging `origin/main` (the first
  derivation warned STALE TREE): 25 commands, all run, all exit 0 — including
  `check:nul-bytes`
  (`scanned 7486 text file(s) ... no raw ASCII control bytes`),
  `check:ratchet-remedy-authority` (`202 scripts swept`),
  `check:declared-population-live`
  (`203 of 254 famil(ies) ... reach this tree's 7493 tracked file(s)`).
  Added by hand beyond the derivation: `check:swallow-census-controls` (exit 0),
  the census's own controls gate.
- Pin tests that read this checker's source:

  (dependency closure built first: a bare run fails on an unbuilt
  `@objectstack/metadata-core`, which reads exactly like a broken import).
- `pnpm lint` — whole repo, `eslint . --no-inline-config`, exit 0. No narrowing,
  so no narrowing evidence is owed.
- No changeset: the diff is `scripts/**` only and publishes nothing. Labelled
